identity.title: ALMA-LEGUS. II. The Influence of Subgalactic Environments on Molecular Cloud Properties

paper_type_evidence.quote: Both galaxies were observed by ALMA (project code 2015.1.00782.S; PI: K. E. Johnson) using Band 6

In this paper, we build upon the analysis of (cite: Finn23a) (hereafter referred to as Paper 1) to further our understanding of how different galactic environments influence the conditions and outcomes of star formation.

findings_qualitative.value: Spiral arms and the center of NGC 7793 have higher masses, linewidths, pressures and virial parameters than interarm and outer regions; surface densities differ little between regions.

evidence.quote: There are higher masses, linewidths, pressures, and virial parameters in the arms of NGC 1313 and center of NGC 7793 than in the interarm and outer regions of the galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: NGC 7793 clouds are as massive and have as much kinetic energy as NGC 1313 arm clouds but lower density and pressure, so are less inclined to collapse.

evidence.quote: Meanwhile NGC 7793 has clouds that are as massive and have as much kinetic energy as clouds in the arms of NGC 1313

claims.hypothesis: Do cloud property variations between regions within a galaxy exceed the variations between the two galaxies globally?
claims.experiment: Compared size-linewidth intercepts, virial plots and cloud property distributions across regions and galaxies
claims.result: Larger regional variation within each galaxy than between galaxies globally, especially in NGC 1313
claims.finding: Local environment influences cloud properties more than global galaxy environment

evidence.quote: We find that there are larger variations in cloud properties between different regions within each galaxy than there are between the galaxies on a global scale, especially for NGC 1313.

claims.hypothesis: Do NGC 1313 spiral arms contain clouds with more kinetic energy than the bar and interarm?
claims.result: Intercepts 0.49 (S arm), 0.40 (N arm) vs 0.32 (bar), 0.27 (interarm); N arm consistent with bar within 3 sigma
claims.finding: Arms have higher kinetic energy than bar or interarm

evidence.quote: These fitted intercepts suggest that the spiral arms of NGC 1313 have higher kinetic energy than the gas in the bar and interarm regions.

claims.hypothesis: Is the NGC 7793 disk uniform in cloud properties apart from its center?
claims.experiment: Regional intercepts, virial plots, distribution comparisons and bootstrapped KS/AD tests
claims.result: All NGC 7793 intercepts consistent within 3 sigma; center has more extreme properties than ring and outer
claims.finding: NGC 7793 disk is relatively uniform, with a more extreme center

evidence.quote: In NGC 7793, the intercepts have a much smaller range than in NGC 1313, and all are consistent with each other within $3\sigma$.

claims.hypothesis: Do arm and interarm regions differ in cloud surface density at 13 pc resolution as at lower resolution?
claims.experiment: Compared clump surface density distributions between regions of NGC 1313
claims.result: Surprisingly little difference in surface density between arm and interarm regions
claims.finding: Lower-resolution surface density contrasts may reflect cloud sparsity (beam filling) rather than true surface density

evidence.quote: We see surprisingly little difference in surface densities between the regions

claims.hypothesis: Is NGC 1313's greater massive cluster formation linked to its greater variety of environments?
claims.experiment: Compared cluster and cloud property variation across regions in both galaxies
claims.result: No single cloud parameter explains the difference; NGC 1313 shows greater regional variation
claims.finding: Massive cluster formation may be driven by NGC 1313's greater variation in environments

evidence.quote: although no one parameter seems primarily responsible for the difference in star formation

why_this_data.value: The two galaxies have similar mass, metallicity, SFR and distance but very different massive cluster populations, making a controlled comparison

evidence.quote: makes the pair an excellent laboratory for directly comparing how the molecular gas conditions and galactic structure affect star cluster formation

why_this_method.value: Dendrograms for size-linewidth and virial analyses (hierarchical scales); clumps for histogram/counting statistics; subsampled KS/AD tests to avoid overpowered statistics

evidence.quote: Dendrograms are hierarchical and include substructure at many size scales, so are preferred for analyses where including the various size scales of the molecular clouds is useful

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Full-sample KS/AD tests rejected as overpowered; two supermassive old clusters in NGC 7793 center disregarded as irrelevant

evidence.quote: Since these overpowered tests are unreliable, we instead perform a bootstrapped version

limitations_admitted.value: Bootstrapped p-values depend strongly on subsample size and cannot establish whether distributions truly differ

evidence.quote: The absolute value of these test results are highly subject to the size of the subsamples used in the bootstrapping

limitations_admitted.value: Fitted slope uncertain, so only intercepts compared with slope held fixed

evidence.quote: These slopes are also often poorly constrained and difficult to compare.

limitations_admitted.value: LEGUS catalogs miss the youngest, highly embedded clusters

evidence.quote: the clusters in the LEGUS catalogs do not include many of the youngest, highly embedded clusters

referee_caveats_inferred: Nearly all inputs (cubes, cloud catalogs, properties) come from Paper 1, so this paper cannot be checked independently
Region boundaries from DSS2-red contours are arbitrary and NGC 7793 regions are by radius, not arms, limiting direct comparison
KS/AD p-values at fixed n=65 are not a calibrated significance test
Intercept comparison depends on the fixed slope 0.5 and on the dendrogram structures chosen
Small sample in NGC 1313 bar (69 clumps) and some regions with few young massive clusters
